title: Proverbs, Chapter 29 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Proverbs 29 on folios 419v, 420r of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Proverbs chapter 29 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folios 419v, 420r.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>אִ֣ישׁ תּ֭וֹכָחוֹת מַקְשֶׁה־עֹ֑רֶף פֶּ֥תַע יִ֝שָּׁבֵ֗ר וְאֵ֣ין מַרְפֵּֽא׃ <sup>2</sup>בִּרְב֣וֹת צַ֭דִּיקִים יִשְׂמַ֣ח הָעָ֑ם וּבִמְשֹׁ֥ל רָ֝שָׁ֗ע יֵאָ֥נַֽח עָֽם׃ <sup>3</sup>אִֽישׁ־אֹהֵ֣ב חָ֭כְמָה יְשַׂמַּ֣ח אָבִ֑יו וְרֹעֶ֥ה ז֝וֹנ֗וֹת יְאַבֶּד־הֽוֹן׃ <sup>4</sup>מֶ֗לֶךְ בְּ֭מִשְׁפָּט יַעֲמִ֣יד אָ֑רֶץ וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּרוּמ֣וֹת יֶֽהֶרְסֶֽנָּה׃ <sup>5</sup>גֶּ֭בֶר מַחֲלִ֣יק עַל־רֵעֵ֑הוּ רֶ֝֗שֶׁת פּוֹרֵ֥שׂ עַל־פְּעָמָֽיו׃ <sup>6</sup>בְּפֶ֤שַֽׁע אִ֣ישׁ רָ֣ע מוֹקֵ֑שׁ וְ֝צַדִּ֗יק יָר֥וּן וְשָׂמֵֽחַ׃ <sup>7</sup>יֹדֵ֣עַ צַ֭דִּיק דִּ֣ין דַּלִּ֑ים רָ֝שָׁ֗ע לֹא־יָבִ֥ין דָּֽעַת׃ <sup>8</sup>אַנְשֵׁ֣י לָ֭צוֹן יָפִ֣יחוּ קִרְיָ֑ה וַ֝חֲכָמִ֗ים יָשִׁ֥יבוּ אָֽף׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy. <sup>2</sup>When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice: but when the wicked beareth rule, the people mourn. <sup>3</sup>Whoso loveth wisdom rejoiceth his father: but he that keepeth company with harlots spendeth his substance. <sup>4</sup>The king by judgment establisheth the land: but he that receiveth gifts overthroweth it. <sup>5</sup>A man that flattereth his neighbour spreadeth a net for his feet. <sup>6</sup>In the transgression of an evil man there is a snare: but the righteous doth sing and rejoice. <sup>7</sup>The righteous considereth the cause of the poor: but the wicked regardeth not to know it. <sup>8</sup>Scornful men bring a city into a snare: but wise men turn away wrath.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>אִֽישׁ־חָכָ֗ם נִ֭שְׁפָּט אֶת־אִ֣ישׁ אֱוִ֑יל וְרָגַ֥ז וְ֝שָׂחַ֗ק וְאֵ֣ין נָֽחַת׃ <sup>10</sup>אַנְשֵׁ֣י דָ֭מִים יִשְׂנְאוּ־תָ֑ם וִֽ֝ישָׁרִ֗ים יְבַקְשׁ֥וּ נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃ <sup>11</sup>כָּל־ר֭וּחוֹ יוֹצִ֣יא כְסִ֑יל וְ֝חָכָ֗ם בְּאָח֥וֹר יְשַׁבְּחֶֽנָּה׃ <sup>12</sup>מֹ֭שֵׁל מַקְשִׁ֣יב עַל־דְּבַר־שָׁ֑קֶר כָּֽל־מְשָׁרְתָ֥יו רְשָׁעִֽים׃ <sup>13</sup>רָ֤שׁ וְאִ֣ישׁ תְּכָכִ֣ים נִפְגָּ֑שׁוּ מֵ֤אִיר־עֵינֵ֖י שְׁנֵיהֶ֣ם יְהוֽ͏ָה׃ <sup>14</sup>מֶ֤לֶךְ שׁוֹפֵ֣ט בֶּֽאֱמֶ֣ת דַּלִּ֑ים כִּ֝סְא֗וֹ לָעַ֥ד יִכּֽוֹן׃ <sup>15</sup>שֵׁ֣בֶט וְ֭תוֹכַחַת יִתֵּ֣ן חָכְמָ֑ה וְנַ֥עַר מְ֝שֻׁלָּ֗ח מֵבִ֥ישׁ אִמּֽוֹ׃ <sup>16</sup>בִּרְב֣וֹת רְ֭שָׁעִים יִרְבֶּה־פָּ֑שַׁע וְ֝צַדִּיקִ֗ים בְּֽמַפַּלְתָּ֥ם יִרְאֽוּ׃
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh, there is no rest. <sup>10</sup>The bloodthirsty hate the upright: but the just seek his soul. <sup>11</sup>A fool uttereth all his mind: but a wise man keepeth it in till afterwards. <sup>12</sup>If a ruler hearken to lies, all his servants are wicked. <sup>13</sup>The poor and the deceitful man meet together: the LORD lighteneth both their eyes. <sup>14</sup>The king that faithfully judgeth the poor, his throne shall be established for ever. <sup>15</sup>The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left to himself bringeth his mother to shame. <sup>16</sup>When the wicked are multiplied, transgression increaseth: but the righteous shall see their fall.

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>יַסֵּ֣ר בִּ֭נְךָ וִֽינִיחֶ֑ךָ וְיִתֵּ֖ן מַעֲדַנִּ֣ים לְנַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃ פ <sup>18</sup>בְּאֵ֣ין חָ֭זוֹן יִפָּ֣רַֽע עָ֑ם וְשֹׁמֵ֖ר תּוֹרָ֣ה אַשְׁרֵֽהוּ׃ <sup>19</sup>בִּ֭דְבָרִים לֹא־יִוָּ֣סֶר עָ֑בֶד כִּֽי־יָ֝בִ֗ין וְאֵ֣ין מַעֲנֶֽה׃ <sup>20</sup>חָזִ֗יתָ אִ֭ישׁ אָ֣ץ בִּדְבָרָ֑יו תִּקְוָ֖ה לִכְסִ֣יל מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃ <sup>21</sup>מְפַנֵּ֣ק מִנֹּ֣עַר עַבְדּ֑וֹ וְ֝אַחֲרִית֗וֹ יִהְיֶ֥ה מָנֽוֹן׃ <sup>22</sup>אִֽישׁ־אַ֭ף יְגָרֶ֣ה מָד֑וֹן וּבַ֖עַל חֵמָ֣ה רַב־פָּֽשַׁע׃ <sup>23</sup>גַּאֲוַ֣ת אָ֭דָם תַּשְׁפִּילֶ֑נּוּ וּשְׁפַל־ר֝֗וּחַ יִתְמֹ֥ךְ כָּבֽוֹד׃ <sup>24</sup>חוֹלֵ֣ק עִם־גַּ֭נָּב שׂוֹנֵ֣א נַּפְשׁ֑וֹ אָלָ֥ה יִ֝שְׁמַ֗ע וְלֹ֣א יַגִּֽיד׃
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>Correct thy son, and he shall give thee rest; yea, he shall give delight unto thy soul. <sup>18</sup>Where there is no vision, the people perish: but he that keepeth the law, happy is he. <sup>19</sup>A servant will not be corrected by words: for though he understand he will not answer. <sup>20</sup>Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him. <sup>21</sup>He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child shall have him become his son at the length. <sup>22</sup>An angry man stirreth up strife, and a furious man aboundeth in transgression. <sup>23</sup>A man's pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit. <sup>24</sup>Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and bewrayeth it not.

translation.original_text: <sup>25</sup>חֶרְדַּ֣ת אָ֭דָם יִתֵּ֣ן מוֹקֵ֑שׁ וּבוֹטֵ֖חַ בַּיהוָ֣ה יְשֻׂגָּֽב׃ <sup>26</sup>רַ֭בִּים מְבַקְשִׁ֣ים פְּנֵי־מוֹשֵׁ֑ל וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה מִשְׁפַּט־אִֽישׁ׃ <sup>27</sup>תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת צַ֭דִּיקִים אִ֣ישׁ עָ֑וֶל וְתוֹעֲבַ֖ת רָשָׁ֣ע יְשַׁר־דָּֽרֶךְ׃ פ
translation.text: <sup>25</sup>The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe. <sup>26</sup>Many seek the ruler's favour; but every man's judgment cometh from the LORD. <sup>27</sup>An unjust man is an abomination to the just: and he that is upright in the way is abomination to the wicked.
